title: Heinemann Park bands and the riverboat with Fate Marable
summary: His father left the boys by the band at ball games, and his parents took them on the steamer to hear Fate Marable's band, with Red Allen recalled.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Ridgely, uh, last time I saw him was crippled. He must have had a stroke or something. And, uh, I remembered him. Of course, he didn't remember me. I was just a fan, you know. I used to, my father used to take me to ball games on Sunday morning. They were ball games at the old ballpark here, Heinemann Park it was. And he'd take my second brother and I and just let us in the vicinity of the band, you see. They'd have this band playing. It was a tuxedo. And we would sit there and he could roam all over that park. When he came back, he knew where to find us. We would be right by that band. And the same thing goes for the steam of capital. And there may have been other boats that I don't remember the names of, but, uh, Faint Marables band was playing. And I remember my mother and father used to go on there and go on to dance. You know, they appreciated the music too, but I was... Did the radio mothers play anything? No, no. My mother, but not my father. My mother was a pianist. But they would take us on the boat. We were small children and they could just put us by the band, you know. And we were there all night just listening and watching these fellas play. And I remember... And the super time of old years then? Yeah, I remember Faint Marable very well. And, uh, I can remember Red Allen. And I think Louie was a little before me on that boat. I remember he... I remember reading of him being on the boat, but I don't think I ever saw Louie because I would have remembered him. And the other fellas I don't remember. But I remember Red, Allen, and, uh, Faint.
